findings.title: A sale of WHITE or ARGUS that pays the listed pool through take leaves the sell charge to the PoolManager, the Arc PoolManager holds about 107,000 USD of ARGUS, and no other priced currency on the 21 networks charges the sender
findings.difference: The cause is the token contract in both cases. Neither Ethereum nor Arc adds a network property. WHITE 0x9cdf242ef7975d8c68d5c1f5b6905801699b1940 on Ethereum debits the sender 10 percent on top of the amount when the recipient is its Uniswap v2 pair with USDC 0x6ec94f50cadcc79984463688de42a0ca696ec2db or its Uniswap v3 pool with WETH 0xf8f6191561997010870056fc265d0f7ddaf105bf (fee 0.3 percent). The v3 pool is a second charged recipient that F-092 did not list. ARGUS 0xece5ca8bf9220718e5727754026757512212cb3c on Arc debits the sender 1 percent on top when the recipient is its mainPool() 0x6a3bacaa6493734c1ac221ebf42cf530a96c1e02, a Uniswap v3 pool with USDC at fee 1 percent. ARGUS reports currentTaxes() = (100, 100) basis points, taxExpiry() = 0 and isExempt(PoolManager) = false.
findings.mechanism: 1. take debits the caller by amount and then calls transfer(to, amount) on the token (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). The transfer routine checks only that the call did not revert and returned nothing or true (src/types/Currency.sol:60-88). No line compares the fall of the PoolManager balance with the amount. 2. Sweep of this cycle: a measuring stub placed at the PoolManager address by state override (eth_call only) sent one third of the balance of every priced currency to every candidate recipient and read the balances before and after. 13,001 priced currencies on 21 networks, 12,751 with a balance of at least 3 base units, 128,687 recipient trials, 127,554 accepted, 43,808 of them to a v2 style pair, a v3 style pool or a pair listed by DexScreener. Recipients came from getPair and getPool of 83 factories (v2 style, Solidly style and v3 style, each verified on chain) against up to 13 base tokens per network, from every address that a zero argument call of any selector of the token returns, from DexScreener pair lists for currencies above 50 USD, and from four fixed recipients (a plain account, the token itself, the dead address, the wrapped native contract). 3. Result: the PoolManager balance fell by more than the amount for 86 currencies. For 84 of them the excess is 1 to 536 base units (Aave and Compound receipt tokens and valTUSD), which is rounding. The two others are WHITE and ARGUS. 4. WHITE at Ethereum block 26,479,738 on two endpoints: a transfer of 16,088,490.01 WHITE from the PoolManager to the v2 pair lowers its balance by 17,697,339.01 (110.0000 percent) and the pair receives 100 percent. skim(PoolManager) on the pair then returns 16,088,490.01 in full, so the net loss is 1,608,849.00 WHITE. The same transfer to the v3 pool also costs 110.0000 percent. A transfer from either pool to the PoolManager arrives in full, and a transfer from a plain holder to the PoolManager carries no charge. 5. ARGUS at Arc block 32,779,722 on two endpoints: a transfer of 15,539,568.77 ARGUS to the v3 pool lowers the PoolManager balance by 101.0000 percent of the amount. The pool has no skim. A transfer from the pool to the PoolManager arrives at 99.0000 percent. A transfer from a plain holder to the PoolManager carries no charge. 6. Who gains. A holder that sells into the listed pool from its own address pays the amount plus the charge: in the trial a plain holder that sent WHITE to either pool paid 110.0000 percent of the amount, and one that sent ARGUS to its pool paid 101.0000 percent. A caller that pays the amount into the PoolManager, or buys it in a v4 pool, and names the listed pool as recipient of take owes the PoolManager the amount only, and the token takes the charge from the pooled balance. The caller keeps the charge it would have paid: 10 percent of a WHITE sale and 1 percent of an ARGUS sale. Arc transaction 0x471fafc3a4761f749412e3856fac067b8f95e73d1d7bf6240dee396e9fc3e9fb (block 32,766,474) shows the pattern: the contract 0x4d680e3a362f64005b4f71004fdfebe203b0ea59 swaps in v4, the PoolManager sends 3,161.80 ARGUS to the v3 pool and 31.62 ARGUS to the token contract, and the pool pays 7.200687 USDC to the PoolManager. 7. Cost of doing it without a real sale. WHITE: take to the v2 pair, sync, skim to the PoolManager and settle costs gas only and moves 10 percent of the taken amount to the token owner 0x287ecebd1223e235b929217fe596c905a11752ae. One round can take at most 10/11 of the balance, so each round removes at most 1/11 of it and 48 rounds leave about 1 percent ((10/11)^48 = 0.0103). The caller gains nothing from this unless it is the token owner. ARGUS: the return leg loses 1 percent to the buy charge and each v3 swap pays the 1 percent pool fee, so a round trip costs the caller about 3 percent of the amount to remove 1 percent from the PoolManager. 8. History. The cycle 6 scan counted 766 charge transfers and 6,129,406.68 WHITE up to block 26,459,964. No charge transfer followed up to block 26,479,742 (eth_getLogs on one endpoint; the second endpoint refused the range), and balanceOf(PoolManager) is still 48,265,470.022830203421280226 WHITE, the value cycle 6 recorded. For ARGUS two more charge transfers of 59.24 ARGUS in total followed between blocks 32,673,464 and 32,779,791 on two endpoints, which brings the total to 1,297 transfers and 188,066.52 ARGUS.
findings.impact: ARGUS: the PoolManager holds 46,618,706.31 ARGUS, about 107,300 USD at the DefiLlama price of 0.002302 USD (DexScreener: 0.002293 USD, 222,906 USD of liquidity in the listed v3 pool, 53,316 USD of volume in 24 hours). The v4 pools of ARGUS, among them the hookless pool 0xb3f441e8871840ecfcb284e5cbb5b9c21a50e961e1c50109bdced25e429f00cc (USDC and ARGUS, fee 0.985 percent, tick spacing 99, no hook, 90,823 USD of liquidity at DexScreener), together record 188,066.52 ARGUS (about 433 USD) more than the PoolManager holds, assuming no other flow outside pool accounting, and the gap grows by 1 percent of every amount taken straight to the listed pool. The gain goes to the caller of each such route as a saved charge, and the loss falls on the liquidity providers who withdraw last. WHITE: the PoolManager holds 48,265,470.02 WHITE, about 1,495 USD at the DefiLlama price of 0.00003098 USD. Any account can move nearly all of it to the token owner at the cost of gas, and any seller into the two listed pools can let the PoolManager pay the 10 percent charge. Nothing else was found: 19 networks have no priced currency with a sender charge above rounding. The sweep covers priced currencies only. The unpriced token T on BNB Smart Chain that F-092 mentions was not retested.
findings.preconditions: A v4 pool of the token with a balance at the PoolManager, and a caller that names a listed pool as recipient of take. Both hold today. The lists of charged recipients are set by the token owners. I did not check which deployed routers pass a pool address as the recipient of take on their own.
findings.mitigations: Routers and interfaces should take these two tokens to their own address and pay the pool from there, so that the sender of the sale carries the charge. Interfaces should flag a currency when a simulated transfer from the PoolManager to one of its pools lowers the PoolManager balance by more than the amount. Liquidity providers in WHITE and ARGUS pools should expect a shortfall on withdrawal. The deployer cannot close this in core without a balance check around the transfer in take.

findings.title: Any account can call claimFor on the MortgageFi vault share mf-e-usdc-cbbtc for the PoolManager on Base, which adds 2.58 shares to the pooled balance that the caller can book through sync and settle
findings.difference: mf-e-usdc-cbbtc 0xe443cadb4a4fa403caee0e0546c33baff32c51f8 (name mortgagefi-earn-usdc-cbbtc, 6 decimals) is a vault share on Base that pays accrued yield as new shares. Its function claimFor(address), selector 0xddeae033, pays the yield of any holder, and the caller does not have to be that holder. The cause is the token. Base adds no network property.
findings.mechanism: 1. sync stores balanceOf(PoolManager) for a currency and needs no permission (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). _settle credits the caller with the rise of that balance since the sync (src/PoolManager.sol:349-365). 2. An eth_call from the unrelated addresses 0x00000000000000000000000000000000000a11ce and 0x00000000000000000000000000000000000b0b01, through a forwarding stub placed at the caller by state override, ran claimFor(PoolManager) at Base blocks 61,347,858 and 61,347,864 on two endpoints. balanceOf(PoolManager) went from 98.714225 to 101.294415 shares, a rise of 2.580190. claimFor for an address without shares leaves the PoolManager balance unchanged. 3. A caller that runs sync(token), claimFor(PoolManager) and settle inside one unlock is credited 2.580190 shares and can take them. I did not run that sequence against the deployed PoolManager, the statement follows from the two source ranges. 4. The yield keeps accruing on the pooled shares, so the step can be repeated later. 5. The same call pattern was run for 5,477 pooled currencies on 17 networks that have a function whose name says it acts for a holder passed as argument, and for every selector of 7,835 priced currencies. This token and the known ibBUSD (F-090) are the only ones where the PoolManager balance of a currency with a market changes. The token uniusd.fun 0xd98a61961ca8a8a53eaf48f2d6d5af5fe134c801 on Base also raises it, through collectTo(address), but that function mints 875 units to any address for any caller, so the token has no backing to lose.
findings.impact: 2.58 shares, about 2.64 USD at the GeckoTerminal price of 1.0214 USD per share, out of 98.71 shares (about 100.83 USD) that the PoolManager holds for the hookless pool 0x620bc43c2198b61932b13aabbfdba4f6e0b236d6dca7282711277856175b0895 (USDC and mf-e-usdc-cbbtc, fee 0.01 percent, tick spacing 1, no hook; the pool id equals the hash of these five values). The yield belongs to the liquidity providers of that pool in economic terms. They cannot claim it, and any account can.
findings.preconditions: Accrued yield on the shares held by the PoolManager. It is 2.58 shares today.
findings.mitigations: Liquidity providers should not hold yield paying vault shares in a pool when the yield can be claimed for a holder by anyone. Interfaces can flag receipt tokens that have claimFor(address).

cleared.check: Can the full amount be brought back to the PoolManager at no cost after a charged transfer of WHITE or ARGUS
cleared.result: WHITE: yes through the v2 pair, where skim(PoolManager) returns 100 percent and a transfer from the pair arrives in full. The v3 pool has no skim, and a transfer from it arrives in full, so the way back through the v3 pool costs two swap fees of 0.3 percent. ARGUS: no. The v3 pool has no skim and a transfer from it to the PoolManager arrives at 99 percent.

leads.question: Run the charged transfer test of this unit on the unpriced currencies with the most Transfer logs at the PoolManager, starting with token T 0x4ef42e4cf51cd779e9947db65b629ecd8c92b1da on BNB Smart Chain and with every pooled token that answers mainPool(), pair() or uniswapV2Pair() with an address that has code.
leads.why: The sweep covered the 13,001 priced currencies only. T charges 3 percent on top and has no price, and a token that gains a market later would carry the same rule into pools that are already open.

leads.question: Do the deployed Universal Router versions and the common aggregators pass a v2 pair or v3 pool as the recipient of take when a route goes from a v4 pool into a v2 or v3 pool, and how much ARGUS and WHITE volume takes that path per day?
leads.why: When routers do this on their own, ordinary swaps charge the PoolManager without any intent, and the rate of the ARGUS shortfall follows from routed volume. 1,297 charge transfers exist on Arc and 766 on Ethereum.

leads.question: List the tokens created by the ARGUS portal 0x0f1c7cb26d6cd36bd4189e41947658b39437587a and its implementation 0x122c82cfca7a3a2227285cc21f4522e8f551db3a, and test each one that has a v4 pool for the 1 percent sender charge on a transfer to its mainPool().
leads.why: ARGUS is a minimal proxy of a launchpad implementation that has initialize, graduate and setMainPool functions. A second graduated token with a v4 pool would leak in the same way.

leads.question: Build selector files for the full currency lists of Robinhood Chain, World Chain and MegaETH and run the holder argument trial by function name on them.
leads.why: The full list trial ran on 17 networks. On these three only the priced currencies were tried, 491 on Robinhood Chain, 89 on World Chain and 11 on MegaETH.

leads.question: Which pooled tokens can be burned or converted for a holder through a separate migrator, staking or vault contract that is not the token or its implementation?
leads.why: The trials call the token and its implementation only. A migrator with migrateFor(holder) that holds a burn role on the old token would not be seen.

leadResults.answer: Tested on all 21 networks for 13,001 priced currencies with 128,687 recipient trials. WHITE on Ethereum (10 percent, v2 pair and v3 pool, full return through skim on the v2 pair) and ARGUS on Arc (1 percent, v3 pool, return arrives at 99 percent) are the only priced currencies that charge the sender above rounding. ARGUS is worth about 107,300 USD at the PoolManager. The seller that routes through take gains the charge, and the liquidity providers lose it.

Every selector of 7,835 priced currencies above 1 USD that cycle 6 had not covered was called with the PoolManager as argument (636,744 trials), and 5,477 currencies of the full lists with a holder argument function name were tried (9,855 trials). ibBUSD on BNB Smart Chain stays the only token whose pooled balance a stranger can lower. One new token raises it: mf-e-usdc-cbbtc on Base, 2.58 shares through claimFor. The four other Alpaca vault tokens that the BNB Smart Chain PoolManager holds (ibBNB, ibUSDT, ibALPACA, ibCAKE) have no claimFor, and no call changed their pooled balance. Closed lending vaults were not picked out as a group, they were tried as part of the lists.

Applied as a method rule: this unit made no log query on BNB Smart Chain and checked each of its two log counts against a second endpoint or against a balance. The earlier results that the lead names, the sNVB rebase history and the 393 rows of cycle 5, were not repeated here.
